correctness.rationale: The supercritical column-stochastic two-type mean matrix has a positive Perron vector, yielding the unique positive Poisson survival fixed point by strict subhomogeneity. The identity lambda D M q= -(1-q)log(1-q)<q bounds the Jacobian spectral radius below one, legitimizing implicit differentiation and det A>0. The sensitivity matrix identity gives strict negative averaged derivative when d>0; type ordering follows by symmetry and continuation without crossing. In the s=1 rank-one family q2 strictly decreases across the threshold 1-1/lambda, yielding the unique q1 maximum. The scalar root equation is strictly monotone on x>log(lambda). The quadratic coefficient follows from the exact derivative. Standalone code verified 148 tests; finite tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Fixed total migration is a natural controlled quantity in structured mutant establishment; an all-supercritical theorem determines its precise directional bias effect rather than reusing the weak-selection source expansion. The rank-one family represents complete redistribution of offspring independently of parental deme; the unique interior favored-origin optimum exposes an actionable conflict between optimization for a targeted introduction and average establishment. The exact quadratic curvature gives the sensitivity near balanced exchange. The result is structural, motivated and nonimplied by the inspected published leading-order formula.
